summary: Doureth Water Solutions, Inc. (client, Buyer) is acquiring the municipal and industrial water treatment chemicals business of Routand Chemical Company (Seller) under an Asset Purchase Agreement. The business includes a coagulant, sodium hypochlorite and corrosion-inhibitor blending plant in Lake Charles, Louisiana. The $86.4M price is paid in three parts: cash at closing, an $8.64M indemnity escrow, and a $12M seller note. Routand keeps its industrial cleaning chemicals division and will supply caustic soda feedstock to Doureth under a transitional supply side letter. Four problems are planted in the folder. (1) Recovery for general representation claims, including environmental, is limited to an escrow that releases at nine months, although the APA says those representations survive eighteen months. (2) Assumed Liabilities is defined to include pre-Closing environmental liabilities, and Doureth's indemnity of Routand for them is carved out of the cap. The signed LOI said Routand would retain them. (3) The supply side letter lets Routand assign freely, including to a competitor. (4) The Seller Note chooses New York law and Manhattan courts, and the APA's precedence clause lets the Note control enforcement and set-off. That splits indemnity and set-off disputes away from the APA's Delaware Chancery forum.

facts.key: LOI allocation of pre-Closing environmental liabilities

issues.label: indemnity survival gap
issues.description: APA Section 9.1 says General Representations, including the Section 4.12 environmental representation, survive 18 months after the Closing Date. APA Section 9.4(b) makes the Escrow Fund the sole and exclusive source of recovery for Losses under Section 9.2(a), excluding only Fundamental Representations and fraud. Escrow Agreement Section 4.1 releases all remaining Escrow Funds to Routand nine months after the Closing Date. Only amounts covered by Claim Notices delivered before that date are held back. Neither document alone shows the problem. Read together, any general-representation claim first discovered in months 10 to 18 has no source of recovery. That cuts the 18-month survival period to about nine months in practice. Environmental contamination at a chemical blending plant is exactly the kind of issue that tends to surface late. The APA states no release date, so its precedence clause (Section 12.4) does not resolve the conflict.
detect_terms: sole and exclusive source of recovery
issues.expected_finding: Because APA Section 9.4(b) limits Doureth's recovery for general-representation breaches to the Escrow Fund, and Escrow Agreement Section 4.1 releases that fund nine months after Closing, the 18-month survival of the General Representations (including environmental) is effectively cut to nine months. The fix is to extend the escrow release to match the survival period, or to allow recovery beyond the escrow (for example by set-off against the Seller Note) for claims made after release.
detect_terms2: nine (9) months after the Closing Date

issues.label: uncapped indemnity
issues.description: APA Section 2.3(c) defines Assumed Liabilities to include all Liabilities under Environmental Laws relating to the Purchased Assets or the Lake Charles Facility, whether arising before, at or after the Closing. APA Section 9.3(b) requires Doureth to indemnify the Seller Parties for all Assumed Liabilities. APA Section 9.5(c) states that the cap and basket in Section 9.5(a) do not apply to claims under Section 9.3(b). Read together, these provisions leave Doureth with unlimited liability, owed to Routand, for historical contamination at a chemical plant it did not operate. This reverses the signed Letter of Intent (Paragraph 4), under which Routand retained pre-Closing environmental liabilities. The APA's integration and precedence clauses mean the LOI does not cure the problem.
detect_terms: whether arising prior to, at or after the Closing
shall not apply to claims under Section 9.3(b)
issues.expected_finding: Because Section 2.3(c) makes pre-Closing environmental liabilities Assumed Liabilities and Section 9.5(c) exempts Doureth's Section 9.3(b) indemnity for Assumed Liabilities from the cap, Doureth faces unlimited liability for Routand's historical contamination, contrary to the LOI. Pre-Closing environmental liabilities should be moved to Excluded Liabilities, or the uncapped indemnity limited to liabilities arising after Closing.

issues.label: unrestricted assignment
issues.description: The transitional supply side letter governs Routand's 24-month supply of caustic soda feedstock to Doureth, including Doureth's binding monthly volume forecasts and customer-driven demand data. Section 7 lets Routand assign the letter and all its rights and obligations to any Person without Doureth's consent. Doureth's own assignment requires Routand's consent. Routand could therefore transfer the supply relationship, and Doureth's forecast and pricing information, to a competing water treatment chemicals producer. The APA's anti-assignment clause (Section 12.6) covers only 'this Agreement' and does not reach the side letter. The APA non-compete binds only Routand, not an assignee.
issues.expected_finding: Side Letter Section 7 lets Routand assign the feedstock supply arrangement, together with Doureth's forecasts and pricing, to any person, including a competitor, without Doureth's consent. The side letter should require Doureth's prior written consent to any assignment, at minimum prohibiting assignment to a competitor, with a termination right on change of control.

issues.label: governing law mismatch
issues.description: Seller Note Section 9 chooses New York law and submits Doureth to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in the Borough of Manhattan for any action on the Note. That includes disputes over Doureth's Section 5 right to set off indemnity amounts owed under the APA. APA Sections 12.8 and 12.9 choose Delaware law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the Court of Chancery. APA Section 12.4 provides that the APA prevails over Ancillary Agreements except that the Seller Note controls its payment, set-off and enforcement. Neither document alone shows the problem. Together, the precedence clause lets the Note's New York forum govern. Routand could therefore sue on the Note in Manhattan while Doureth's indemnity claims must proceed in Chancery. That risks a judgment on the Note before Doureth's set-off claims are decided, plus inconsistent rulings and duplicate litigation.
detect_terms: laws of the State of New York
issues.expected_finding: The Seller Note's New York governing law and exclusive Manhattan forum conflict with the APA's Delaware law and exclusive Chancery forum, and APA Section 12.4 makes the Note control enforcement and set-off. Indemnity and set-off disputes would therefore be split across two forums under two laws, putting Doureth's set-off right at risk. The Note should be conformed to Delaware law and the Chancery forum, or the Section 12.4 exception removed.
